company.name: RankClaw
company.description: Security scanner for AI agent skills — indexes and AI-deep-audits skills in the OpenClaw/ClawHub ecosystem (Claude-based agents with file, web, shell access). Found 1,103 malicious skills out of 14,706 (7.5%).

founder.contact: unknown — find via rankclaw.com or HN profile

signal.title: Show HN: RankClaw – AI-audited all 14,706 OpenClaw skills; 1,103 are malicious

why_pp_matters: RankClaw solves the pre-deploy trust problem (can we trust this skill was designed safely?). PP solves the complementary runtime problem (what is this skill permitted to DO once deployed?). Two non-overlapping layers. Partnership angle: RankClaw clears deployment, PP enforces execution scope. Our comment on their HN post raises exactly this — generative payloads (lekt9/foundry) mean static+AI audit doesn't structurally close the loop. Runtime scope enforcement is the missing piece they can't build into a scanner.
attack_patterns_found: Prompt injection in SKILL.md natural language (scored 95/100 shallow, 38/100 AI audit)
On-demand RCE via challenge evaluation (server picks payload type at call time)
LLM-generated payload (no malicious code at audit time — AI writes it during conversation)
Social engineering script in SKILL.md ('Can I mine Bonero?')

engagement.angle: AI audit catches what shallow heuristics miss; still doesn't constrain runtime scope. Pre-declared tool grants + enforcement independent of agent are the two missing defenses. Closed the loop with a question about capability distribution (file vs shell vs network).
